title: ConcordAI - embedding cascade, rerank and hosting paths discovery
summary: Initial discovery for ConcordAI focused on embedding dimensionality, cascade/rerank design, and which hosting path (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) makes sense given throughput & compliance needs. Customer wants a pilot to validate tail latency and rerank precision at 200 qps hybrid fanout with a 1s p95 target. Security and KMS are gating items.
topics: vector DB integration options and sharding
next_steps: Redwood to share hosting option comparison + pricing grid by 2029-11-08
Redwood SE to send benchmark template and request sample query set by 2029-11-07
Customer to confirm dataset size and expected qps by 2029-11-09
Schedule pilot kick-off workshop (30m) week of 2029-11-12

Priya: prepare benchmark spreadsheet + suggested config rows (due 2029-11-07)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-11-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Marcus (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jonah (Redwood Solutions); Elena, Tom, Ravi, Sofia (ConcordAI)

[00:00] Marcus: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Marcus from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer, and Jonah who helps with pilots.
[00:07] Elena: Hi, thanks. I'm Elena, I run search at ConcordAI. We have Ravi on ML and Tom is infra, Sofia from security.
[00:12] Marcus: Great. Quick agenda — we want to understand your current embedding pipeline, fanout/rerank needs, constraints, and what hosting mode you're leaning to. We'll then talk about pilot options.
[00:23] Ravi: Quick context: we run a hybrid retrieval system. First stage is a vector DB fanout for top 200, then a reranker model on text/sparse signals. Looking to move rerank off our GPUs to a managed solution because ops are killing us — so throughput and tail latency are the big concerns.
[00:37] Priya: Right, and are you currently using any vector DB?
[00:40] Tom: We're on an in-house service backed by Milvus for storage, but it's stretched. We've tried Pinecon — Pinecone — for spikes but the costs get weird. We're also exploring co-locating embeddings in our app infra.
[00:53] Marcus: Understood. Two immediate design questions we usually surface: do you want the rerank to live close to your vector DB (co-located) or as a separate inference path? And second, are you open to quantized embeddings and model variants for cost reduction?
[01:07] Elena: We want to preserve accuracy; recall and re-rank precision matter for our top-k. But we also need to justify unit economics. Our stakeholder has a 1s p95 SLA for the end-to-end query. The vector fanout expansion is often 150-300 depending on query.
[01:22] Priya: Okay. To hit 1s p95 for the full stack, we typically recommend a cascade: reduce fanout with a fast approximate embed match, then do a small high-quality rerank on the top N. That keeps token costs and latency in check.
[01:34] Ravi: How small does N need to be? We worry about losing recall if N is too low. Most of our failure cases are in the long tail queries.
[01:40] Priya: From our experience, trying N=20-50 for the high-quality reranker gets you most of the lift with far lower compute. But it depends on embedding dimensionality and the vector DB recall. Also quantization has improved — like 8-bit or even 4-bit embeddings in some pipelines — but you need to validate for your metrics.
[01:56] Tom: Can Redwood serve the rerank model directly and call our vector DB? Or do we push vectors into Redwood's store?
[02:03] Jonah: Both patterns are supported. You can keep a vector DB in your VPC and route rerank requests to Redwood Private/Dedicated via VPC peering or private link, or you can push embeddings to our hosted store and use our fast fanout + rerank. Tradeoffs: hosting keeps latency predictable and offloads ops; private keeps data residency and network control.
[02:20] Elena: Our security team will want KMS and audit logs. We can't push certain PII out of our VPC for now.
[02:26] Sofia: Yeah we need to see key management and the SOC2 report. Also ability to rotate keys and a detailed audit trail.
[02:31] Marcus: Totally. We'll share our SOC2 + ISO artifacts and our KMS integration doc. For PII you'd likely lean Dedicated or Private with bring-your-own-key (BYOK).
[02:39] Ravi: What's the expected throughput and cost difference? Say we target 200 qps sustained during peak and 300 qps bursts.
[02:46] Priya: If you go Hosted with our managed vector store and rerank, the ops are simplest but costs can be higher per qps. Dedicated reserved pools get you far better unit economics at scale — and Private gives you the most control but more setup. We can share a price-per-100qps grid.
[03:01] Elena: For the pilot, we want to test the rerank precision delta between dim=1536 and dim=768 and also try 8-bit quantized embeddings. We also want to run tail latency benchmarks at 200 qps to simulate production.
[03:14] Priya: Makes sense. We'll propose a benchmark matrix: dims {1536, 1024, 768}, quantization off/on, rerank topN {20, 50, 100}, and measure p50/p95/p99 end-to-end.
[03:25] Tom: Note our doc corpus is ~120M documents, but the active shard for search is around 35M with average doc vector size ~1536 dims. Cardinality for the typical fanout is high — a lot of near-neighbors.
[03:38] Jonah: 120M across entire corpus is fine, for the pilot we can sample the 35M hot set. We'll need a sample dump for indexing and an expected update rate.
[03:45] Ravi: Update rate's about 50k updates/day, with bulk reindex windows every weekend.
[03:51] Priya: That update cadence affects how often you re-quantize or re-index. If you're doing frequent updates, push-then-serve vs hybrid will differ.
[03:59] Elena: Also curious about sharding. We're hitting hotspots depending on user segments. Does Redwood do automatic shard rebalancing or is that on the DB side?
[04:07] Marcus: For Hosted, we handle sharding and placement; we recommend sharding by prefix or logical partition. For Private you usually manage your DB shards and Redwood routes to the appropriate shard. Dedicated's a middle ground — we operate the pool but you can bring your sharded DB behind a private endpoint.
[04:21] Tom: Any notes on tail latency mitigation? We see outliers when rerank model cold-starts and KV cache isn't warmed.
[04:28] Priya: We have warm cache strategies, continuous batching, and a KV cache for LLAMA-style kvs, but for embedding rerank specifically we recommend warm pools and prewarming on predictable traffic patterns. Also experimental techniques like approximate prefiltering reduce tail.
[04:42] Ravi: Does Redwood support quantized model variants in the reranker? Like 4-bit LLMs or distilled rerankers?
[04:48] Priya: Yes, our runtime supports quantized kernels and distillation-based rerankers. We can run a smaller model variant for the low-latency path and fall back to bigger model for edge cases. We also support A/B rollouts and automatic fallback when latency SLOs are at risk.
[05:03] Elena: How about integration friction? We don't want a long integration — timeline is 6 weeks to pilot.
[05:09] Marcus: Typical pilot can be 4–8 weeks. Week 0: data handoff and config. Week 1–2: index + smoke tests. Week 3: benchmark run. Week 4: analysis and tuning. We'll provide a pilot checklist.
[05:20] Tom: What network setup options for Private? VPC peering vs private link, and can we put the inference nodes in our subnet?
[05:27] Jonah: For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane and can deploy inference nodes in your VPC (air-gapped option available in enterprise). For Dedicated we offer private endpoints; for Hosted it's public endpoints with VPC egress options.
[05:39] Sofia: And for KMS — can we use our HSM or do you require a particular vendor?
[05:44] Marcus: We integrate with common cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and support BYOK workflows; HSM integrations are part of the Private package. We'll share the technical note.
[05:54] Elena: On metrics, we need token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, and rerank quality metrics. Is that in Redwood Console?
[06:02] Priya: Yes, Console exposes cost per token, per model, and tracing hooks so you can see per-request breakdowns. We'll also surface evals against your golden prompts.
[06:11] Ravi: About vector DB integration — if we keep Milvus, how does Redwood connect and what about consistent top-k between the two systems?
[06:18] Priya: You'd keep Milvus as the ground-truth store. Redwood can call your Milvus endpoints for fanout and then run rerank on the returned candidates. The top-k consistency depends on similarity function and indexing method; we'll want to validate recall during pilot. Usually you see minor differences because of index params, but you can tune index parameters or use hybrid mixing.
[06:35] Tom: Any constraints on vector dims? We might explore sparse + dense combos (sparse signals plus dense vectors).
[06:41] Priya: No hard constraint — runtime supports dense vectors up to 4096 dims but costs grow linearly. Hybrid sparse + dense is common: use BM25-like signals first stage, dense second stage, or vice versa.
[06:52] Elena: For the pilot, we'd like Redwood to test two topologies: (A) keep Milvus in VPC + Redwood rerank in Private mode; (B) push a reduced-size sample index into Redwood Hosted and run full fanout+rerank. Compare latency, recall, and cost.
[07:06] Marcus: That's a good A/B. We'll capture that as pilot plan.
[07:10] Priya: We'll need sample index snapshot (s3 link) and 1k-5k typical queries plus workload shape to simulate qps.
[07:17] Ravi: We'll provide 1k queries and a 1M doc sample to start. We can't send full 35M for the first run.
[07:22] Marcus: Great. A few gotchas we usually call out: 1) embedding dim reductions sometimes change nearest neighbor structure; validate metrics; 2) quantization can bias distances; 3) network egress and VPC topology will affect p95.
[07:36] Elena: Noted. Also procurement question: if we go Dedicated what's commitment length?
[07:41] Marcus: Dedicated is typically reserved monthly or annual commits; for pilots customers sometimes run a month of Dedicated with a pilot discount or run a Hosted pilot and then convert. We'll put options in the pricing grid.
[07:52] Tom: On caching at the rerank layer — can Redwood cache rerank results for repeat queries? We have user sessions with many repeat queries.
[07:59] Priya: Yes, we support prefix caching and result caching; you can set TTLs by route. There's also a KV cache for model state to reduce cold-starts.
[08:10] Ravi: How are function calls / structured outputs handled in rerank? We sometimes run LLM-augmented reranks that call retrieval tools.
[08:17] Jonah: You can chain tool calls in the request path. For high-throughput rerank we recommend pushing only the minimum fields—i.e., send candidate text ids and fetch in the rerank sandbox to reduce payload.
[08:29] Elena: Anything on SLOs during noisy neighbor events? We need graceful fallback.
[08:34] Priya: We have automatic fallback policies — e.g., if big model exceeds latency budget, route to smaller model variant, or reduce topN dynamically. We'll help set policies during pilot.
[08:46] Marcus: Okay let's go into the benchmark specifics. Priya, can you outline the matrix you proposed?
[08:50] Priya: Sure. Columns: embedding dim, quantized Y/N, vector index type (IVF/HNSW), fanout, rerank topN, model variant (small/medium), route (hosted/dedicated/private). Metrics: latency end-to-end, p95 token, rerank MAP@10, recall@50, cost per 1k queries. We'll run synthetic qps at 50/100/200 with representative query timer distribution.
[09:10] Elena: MAP@10 is our preferred metric. We'll send labeled queries with ground truth.
[09:15] Marcus: We'll also instrument per-request traces and surface where time is spent — network, index, rerank model.
[09:22] Tom: For the routing layer, can Redwood detect capacity and automatically failover to a different region/model?
[09:27] Priya: Yes, smart routing supports model variant fallback, region fallback, and capacity-based routing. You can set policy thresholds.
[09:34] Ravi: One more thing — we use off-the-shelf approximate nearest for indexing; memory per vector is a concern. Any suggestions around compression?
[09:42] Priya: Product recommendations: 1) lower dims where acceptable, 2) quantize embeddings, 3) shard by logical partitions and evict cold shards, 4) use sparse representations for certain fields. We'll suggest quant profiles per workload.
[09:58] Elena: On compliance, can we get an NDA and then share a larger dataset?
[10:02] Marcus: Yes, we'll route NDA through your procurement contact.
[10:07] Sofia: We'll want to engage security with an architecture diagram and threat model before production.
[10:12] Marcus: We'll include a private deployment architecture doc in the follow-up.
[10:16] Elena: What are typical pilot success criteria?
[10:19] Marcus: Typically: 1) meet p95 SLA target (1s) for end-to-end on pilot dataset at target qps, 2) rerank MAP improvement >= baseline, 3) acceptable cost per query relative to target, 4) security sign-off on hosting option.
[10:31] Ravi: We'll add an internal metric about cold-start frequency — can't have more than 2% cold-starts causing >500ms extra latency.
[10:37] Priya: We can surface cold-start traces and propose prewarm schedules.
[10:41] Tom: Any obstacles to running pilot in first two weeks of Nov?
[10:44] Marcus: We can start as soon as we get the samples and the signed pilot SOW.
[10:49] Elena: We'll try to get the SOW signed fast. Procurement questions: what is the billing cadence?
[10:53] Marcus: Monthly billing for Hosted/Dedicated pilot invoices; Dedicated long-term usually annual but can be shortened for pilot. We'll put terms in SOW.
[11:02] Jonah: Quick note on observability: Console will show per-request token cost, trace, and rerank quality metrics if you feed the golden labels.
[11:10] Ravi: Regarding Milvus integration, do you have a connector or do we stand up a little adapter?
[11:14] Priya: We have an adapter pattern used by other customers—small proxy that translates Redwood fanout calls to Milvus queries. For Private deployments you can keep it in VPC.
[11:23] Tom: Okay. I'm worried about reindex time for 35M docs — would a delta strategy be better?
[11:27] Priya: Yes, delta indexing and snapshotting are recommended. Also hybrid incremental reindexing during low-traffic windows.
[11:33] Elena: Alright wrapping up — can you email the pilot plan and security artifacts?
[11:36] Marcus: Yes. We'll send: pilot plan, benchmark template, pricing grid, SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS doc.
[11:44] Sofia: We'll review and get back.
[11:47] Elena: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[11:50] Marcus: Thanks all — we'll follow up with action items.
[11:53] [meeting ends]
transcription_notes: Occasional mis-hearings: 'KV cash' appears once, product names sometimes transcribed e.g., 'Pinecon' for Pinecone. Speaker labels vary (some lines use first names, some 'Marcus'). Short crosstalk present.
